catalog_citation: Stappers, Leo. 1971. Esquisse de la langue lengola. Africana Linguistica 5 (Annales du Musée Royal de l'Afrique Centrale, Sciences humaines 72), 255-307. DOI 10.3406/aflin.1971.890 (Persée).
catalog_locator: §1.6 'Phonèmes supra-segmentaires : tonèmes', p. 259 (foot of page; page image the copy we hold, scanned the copy we line 306); §1.7 'Phonèmes supra-segmentaires :…
catalog_quote: 1.6. Phonèmes supra-segmentaires : tonèmes. Il y a quatre tonèmes : haut /H/, bas /B/, descendant /D/ et montant /M/. Les deux derniers pourraient être considérés comme composés respectivement d'un tonème bas-haut et d'un tonème haut-bas. [p. 260] 1.7. Phonèmes supra-segmentaires : quantité ... i6ûûna / i6ûna, itóóla / itóla, ééna / éna ... [p. 261] 2.8. Morphotonèmes. Il y a un morphotonème bas (°B) et un morphotonème haut (°H) associés à un morphophonème vocalique ou nasal. Exceptionnellement un morphophonème vocalique porte deux morphotonèmes °N=sêké (°H+B). La représentation de ces morphotonèmes est directe, c'est-à-dire par le tonème correspondant.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: 1.6. Phonèmes supra-segmentaires : tonèmes. Il y a quatre tonèmes : haut /H/, bas /B/, descendant /D/ et montant /M/. Les deux derniers pourraient être considérés comme composés respectivement d'un tonème bas-haut et d'un tonème haut-bas.
new_statements.translation: 1.6. Supra-segmental phonemes: tonemes. There are four tonemes: high /H/, low /B/, falling /D/ and rising /M/. The last two could be regarded as composed respectively of a low-high toneme and a high-low toneme [sic; the order is reversed in the original].
new_statements.citation: Stappers, Leo. 1971. Esquisse de la langue lengola. Africana Linguistica 5 (Annales du Musée Royal de l'Afrique Centrale 72), 255-307. DOI 10.3406/aflin.1971.890.
new_statements.locator: §1.6 'Phonèmes supra-segmentaires : tonèmes', p. 259 (see also §1.7 quantité, p. 260; §2.8 Morphotonèmes, p. 261)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the quoted passage sits at line 306, inside the '===== PAGE 259 =====' block, word for word as the report gives it ("1.6. Phonèmes supra-segmentaires : tonèmes. Il y a quatre tonèmes : haut /H/, bas /B/, descendant /D/ et montant /M/. Les deux derniers pourraient être considérés comme composés respectivement d'un tonème bas-haut et d'un tonème haut-bas."). I also viewed the page image persee_pages/: the printed text at the foot of p. 259 matches the scanned exactly, including the original's reversed order 'bas-haut.. haut-bas' (so the first reader's [sic] is right; it is Stappers' text, not an scanned slip). The scanned file carries all 53 pages 255-307 (page markers checked; p. 256…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lengola is described as a tone language with four tonemes (H, L, falling, rising) plus contrastive vowel length; the sketch contains no statement about word stress or accent at all (the term 'accent' does not occur in the 53 pages).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tone section only notes that falling and rising could be analysed as contour sequences.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone stated at the level of the phoneme inventory; word-level tone patterns given for nominal themes (§4.1) and verb forms (§7-8). No statement on stress at any level.
new_statements.identity_note: Stappers 1971 (p. 257) describes the ilengóla of a single informant, Ali Gabriel (b. 1944, Ponthierville, now Ubundu), from the Balega group of the Balengola (the riverine fishing group along the Lualaba; the other two groups are the Babila and Bavalongo). This is the language-level variety leng1258 (D.12); no separate glottocode for the Balega sub-group.

sources.note: Only two descriptive items: Stappers 1971 (grammar sketch) and Sibatu 1977 (study of one feature, syntax MA thesis). The rest are wordlists (Stuhlmann 1916/17), ethnography (Jak 1938, 1939; Biebuyck 1976, 1977), a regional overview (Bokula et al. 1979) and lexicostatistic/phylogenetic comparative works (Bastin, Coupez & Mann 1999; Grollemund et al. 2015).
